title: Vacilando Runtime — command + audit contracts (v1)
description: The contract for the Vacilando command runtime: how the loopback control plane turns an operator intent into a toolkit effect, safely. A command is a REGISTERED key mapped to an explicit alloy-* CLI (or an internal read). There is no arbitrary shell, no request-supplied executable path, and no way to run anything not defined in the registry. Consequential commands preview → confirm. Release, promotion, merge, and destructive git are intentionally unsupported.

request.preview: POST /api/commands/preview  { command, input }  → resolve+validate+eligibility+preview; NEVER executes.
request.execute: POST /api/commands  { command, input, confirm, actor }  → runs through the registry after the confirmation policy is satisfied.
notes: `command` must be a registered key; unknown keys → 404 unknown_command.
`input` is validated against the command's declarative schema; unexpected or malformed fields → 400 invalid_input.
`confirm` must be true for consequential commands; otherwise → 428 confirmation_required.
The request never carries an argv, a shell string, or an executable path.

command_definition.bin: FIXED alloy-* basename (cli only); resolved to an absolute path under the toolkit — never from the request
command_definition.input: declarative field schema (types: slot, key, id, name, text); fail-closed
command_definition.buildArgv: pure fn: validated input → argument array (cli only). No string interpolation into a shell.
command_definition.resolveTarget: fn: input + snapshot → the authoritative target record
command_definition.refresh: which authoritative projections to recompute after execution (e.g. ["snapshot"])

registered_commands.runtime.refresh: internal — recompute the projection from authoritative sources.
registered_commands.sprint.inspect: internal read — return the projected sprint/worker/repository slice for a slot.
registered_commands.worker.pause: alloy-worker-pause <slot>  — stop the slot's provider/server/browser (reversible). consequential, confirm.
registered_commands.worker.resume: alloy-worker-resume <slot>  — restore from pause. consequential, confirm.
registered_commands.question.answer: alloy-product-decide <key> <decision-id> --choice <c> --decided-by <n> --reason <r>  — answer a pending question. consequential, confirm; eligible only when an OPEN decision matches.

unsupported.promotion.promote: Human-only; the toolkit prints but never executes push/PR. Release is never auto-approved.
unsupported.repo.push: Not an executable toolkit command (printed, never run).
unsupported.repo.merge: Landing happens through PR review into staging, by a human.
unsupported.worktree.delete: Destructive git/worktree deletion is out of Phase 1 policy; requires explicit human action.

audit.storage: append-only JSONL at <runtime-root>/vacilando/audit.jsonl — an EXECUTION audit, not a parallel state store.

fields.command: the registered command key that ran
fields.input: validated input (secret-shaped keys redacted; long values truncated)

invariants: Unknown command keys and malformed input fail closed.
Commands execute ONLY through explicitly registered adapters over existing alloy-* tooling.
No arbitrary shell: execFile with an argument array, shell disabled; no request-supplied paths.
Consequential commands require preview → explicit confirmation; confirmation cannot be bypassed.
Release, promotion, merge, and destructive git are unsupported — surfaced with a reason, never simulated.
Every execution (and every refusal/block) is audited; the canonical projection refreshes after execution.
The SPA is presentation-only; it holds no orchestration logic and talks only to /api/*.
